# FDG3087

> DO NOT directly expose localizable resources as public (or protected) members.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.8 Naming Resources.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG3087
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Make the resource class '{0}' internal

FDG3087 reports an externally visible class marked [GeneratedCode("System.Resources.Tools.StronglyTypedResourceBuilder", ...)], a resource class that a resource editor generated as public. Resources exposed through hand-written members are not detected. Library profile only: an application's resource classes are not public API, so this rule is off in the application profile.

## From the book

The types and members automatically generated by a resource editor should use the `internal` access modifier.

When it does make sense to expose a resource via public API, use intentional type and member design.
